svg.title: Red eye: red flags decide whether it is vision threatening. Without them it is the lids, a conjunctivitis told apart by its discharge and itch, a subconjunctival hemorrhage or a corneal abrasion; with them it is keratitis, anterior uveitis or acute angle closure glaucoma and needs urgent ophthalmology; each column gives the presentation, the exam finding that decides it and the treatment, and a last column for the other vision threats (orbit, sclera, globe)

svg.text: red flag symptoms: blurred vision that does NOT clear with blinking (clears = discharge) · SEVERE pain (keratitis, ulcer, iritis,

svg.text: scleritis, glaucoma) · photophobia (iritis) · coloured halos (corneal edema, high pressure)

svg.text: red flag signs: ↓ acuity · ciliary flush · corneal opacity · abnormal pupil · shallow chamber · ↑ pressure · proptosis

svg.text: ask: onset, one or both eyes · pain, photophobia · discharge type + amount · itch · vision · recent cold · family member with red

svg.text: eye · contact lenses (swim, sleep, shower in them?) · trauma, eye surgery · eye drops · autoimmune disease
